title: Enhanced digestion of complex cosmetic matrices for analysis of As, Hg, Cd, Cr, Ni, and Pb using triton X-100
author: Maharaj, Mohammed, et al.

steps.title: Prepare glassware
steps.instruction: Wash all glassware with an anionic detergent, rinse with tap water then deionized water, soak in diluted nitric acid for 24 h, rinse again with deionized water and air‑dry at room temperature.

steps.title: Weigh samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.5 ± 0.1 g of each face‑powder or lipstick sample in triplicate into clean, dried, labelled boiling tubes.

steps.title: Add digestion reagents
steps.instruction: Add the acid mixture for the chosen digestion regime (see table below). All reagents are added at the volumes indicated; when Triton X‑100 is used add 1 mL of a 5 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 solution.

substeps.instruction: • Method A‑1: 5 mL 70 % HNO₃, 5 mL 30 % H₂O₂, 1 mL 5 % Triton X‑100 (temperature 95 °C, time 3 h).
• Method B‑1: 7.5 mL 37 % HCl, 7.5 mL 70 % HNO₃ (temperature 108 °C, time 2 h).
• Method C‑1: 8 mL 70 % HNO₃, 4 mL 37 % HCl, 2 mL 30 % H₂O₂ (temperature 125 °C, time 2 h).
• Method A‑2: 5 mL 70 % HNO₃, 5 mL 30 % H₂O₂ (temperature 95 °C, time 3 h).
• Method B‑2: 7.5 mL 37 % HCl, 7.5 mL 70 % HNO₃ (temperature 108 °C, time 2 h).
• Method C‑2: 8 mL 70 % HNO₃, 4 mL 37 % HCl, 2 mL 30 % H₂O₂ (temperature 125 °C, time 2 h).

steps.title: Pre‑digest
steps.instruction: Seal the tubes and let the mixtures stand at room temperature for 24 h.

steps.title: Digest on heating block
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a heating block, raise the temperature to the value specified for the chosen method (95 °C for A, 108 °C for B, 125 °C for C) and maintain for the prescribed time (3 h for A, 2 h for B and C).

steps.title: Cool and filter
steps.instruction: Allow the digests to cool to room temperature, then filter each through Whatman No. 541 filter paper into a 50 mL volumetric flask. Rinse the filter with deionized water and bring the filtrate to the 50 mL mark with deionized water.

steps.title: Arsenic reduction (if required)
steps.instruction: Transfer 5 mL of the 50 mL filtrate to a clean boiling tube, add 5 mL of 1 % potassium iodide in 1 M HCl, let stand for 50 min at room temperature, filter through Whatman No. 541 into a 25 mL volumetric flask and make up to 25 mL with deionized water.

description: The concentrations obtained for the lipstick and face powder samples are shown in Table 3 and Table 5 respectively. For both lipstick and powder samples, the RSD% were below 5% which indicated that the values were close to the average value. As shown in Table 3, the average concentration of As, Cd, Cr, Pb, Hg and Ni using Method A-1 were higher than the average concentrations obtained from Methods B-1, C-1, A-2, B-2 and C-2. Method A-1 extracted all of the heavy metals of interest from the lipstick samples and minimized the loss of the heavy metals. The statistical comparison displayed in Table 4 showed that the average concentration for the heavy metals of interest in lipsticks digested with the addition of Triton X-100 was slightly higher (5.60 ± 12.92 mg/kg) than that recorded without the use of Triton X-100 (5.22 ± 13.62 mg/kg). In both cases, the minimum concentrations were 0.00 mg/kg, while maximum concentrations were 50.52 mg/kg (With Triton X-100) and 56.86 mg/kg (without Triton X-100).
